body:
The reviewed AMOS/Blitz openings make workload-free performance and safety claims. Examples include Blitz unit 1's “compiled code runs many times faster” and unit 3's comparison that an interpreted AMOS number uses a “big, safe box for everything”. The mode lesson also generalises its OS trade to every Amiga game. The included sources/captures demonstrate greetings, graphics and one byte wrap; they supply no comparative timing or whole-language range proof.

Review only the two module overviews and first three units of each track. Preserve the concrete edit/run/compile and storage explanations, but replace general rankings with named mechanisms and explicit boundaries. Treat runtime type/range behaviour as a language contract requiring primary documentation and selected execution, and performance as a processor/language/workload measurement. Do not add invented benchmarks or use a historical generalisation as proof.

Acceptance: retain exact before/after claims and primary citations; any comparative measurement names the same task/configuration and preserves correct results. Keep AMOS and Blitz independent peers. Verify the changed prose and representative rendered pages; no broad rewrite.

Parent: stevehill1981/198x#116. Source audit: Code198x/docs `audit/2026-10-amiga-opening/REPORT.md` (pending review).
title: Qualify the Amiga opening lessons’ speed and representation claims
